# S609 — adj guard check: flag a client passed as an argument or bound with `var`, and an inverted guard

**Findings:**  · **Size:**  · **Tree:**

**2026-11-26** — The checker detects all specified unguarded forms and accepts current engine guards; S609’s formatting check now targets internal/engine and passes.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

The reviewer of ork run ork-20261125-235639-7e56 probed the adj guard test from S570 (`internal/engine/adjguard_test.go`). It found three forms that pass as guarded, although they are not guarded:
- `use(e.d.Adj)`, where the client is passed as an argument.
- `var c = e.d.Adj`.
- `if e.proj.Adj { return }` followed by `e.d.Adj.Check`, where the guard is inverted. `earlyExitGuardBefore` accepts any `if` whose condition reads the bool and whose body exits, with no regard to polarity.

None of these forms occurs in the engine today. S570's client-use definition leaves the first two out, and its early-exit rule accepts the third. They are gaps in the test, not defects in the engine.

The same polarity gap exists in the body rule. `if !e.proj.Adj { e.d.Adj.Check(...) }` passes because `readsAdjBool` ignores `!`. This slice fixes both rules with one polarity-aware condition check, so a guard counts only when the condition implies that the project's `Adj` flag is set. The current engine passes under the stricter rule. Every guard in the tree is `X.Adj` or `!X.Adj`, joined by `&&` or `||` in the polarity-correct way: `decisionpaths.go:60`, `later.go:193`, `engine.go:404`, `brief.go:48`, `speccheck.go:857`, `speccheck.go:923`.

## Implement

1. In `internal/engine/adjguard_test.go`, widen `isAdjClientUse`. In addition to the selector operand and the assignment right-hand side, a `.Adj` selector is a client use when it is one of `Args` of an `*ast.CallExpr`, or one of `Values` of an `*ast.ValueSpec` (covers `var c = e.d.Adj`). The bool-read rule is unchanged: any other `.Adj` selector is a bool read. Add a comment that a bool passed as a call argument would also read as a client use, since the check is syntactic. The tree has no such site.
2. Replace `readsAdjBool` with `condImpliesAdj(cond ast.Expr, whenTrue bool) bool`. It reports whether the condition, evaluating to `whenTrue`, implies the project `Adj` flag is set.
   - `*ast.ParenExpr`: recurse with the same `whenTrue`.
   - `*ast.UnaryExpr` with `!`: recurse with `!whenTrue`.
   - `&&`: when `whenTrue` is true, true if either operand implies it; when false, false.
   - `||`: when `whenTrue` is false, true if either operand implies it; when true, false.
   - A `.Adj` `*ast.SelectorExpr`: return `whenTrue`.
   - Anything else: false.
   - Only operators and parentheses are walked, so a `.Adj` selector reached this way is a bool read. A client expression such as `e.d.Adj != nil` is never descended into.
3. In `adjGuarded`, the `*ast.IfStmt` body case calls `condImpliesAdj(a.Cond, true)`. This accepts `if e.proj.Adj {` and `if f.Key != "" && e.proj.Adj {`, and no longer accepts `if !e.proj.Adj {`.
4. In `earlyExitGuardBefore`, call `condImpliesAdj(ifs.Cond, false)` together with `exitsEarly(ifs.Body)`. Falling through means the condition was false, so this accepts `if !e.proj.Adj { return }` and `if !project.Adj || q.Key == "" { continue }`, and no longer accepts `if e.proj.Adj { return }`.
5. Update the `unguardedAdjCalls` doc comment to state the widened client-use forms and the polarity rule.
6. Add TestAdjGuardFlagsClientArgument, TestAdjGuardFlagsVarBoundClient and TestAdjGuardFlagsInvertedGuard from Failing tests. Follow the table style of TestAdjGuardFlagsUnguardedCall, using `checkAdjSnippet` and asserting the exact `line: func` finding. Add the accept cases to the two existing accept tests.
7. Run `go -C /home/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork test ./internal/engine`. TestEngineAdjCallsAreGuarded must still pass on the real tree. Then run `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l ./internal/engine`.
